body:
Estimated end-of-life date, accurate to within three months: 05-2027
See [the support level definitions](https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/trace_collection/compatibility/python/#releases) for more information.

### Upgrade Notes

- CI Visibility
  - Removes the legacy pytest plugin. The `DD_PYTEST_USE_NEW_PLUGIN` and `DD_PYTEST_USE_NEW_PLUGIN_BETA` environment variables no longer have any effect; the pytest plugin is always used. Remove these environment variables from your configuration to silence the deprecation warning emitted while they are set.
- dd-trace-py 4.17 adds support for **Python 3.15**. Most of the library is tested and ready on 3.15. Some products and integrations are not yet validated on Python 3.15. You can track progress in [\#17809](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-py/issues/17809).

### New Features

- AAP
  - Adds Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) exploit prevention and downstream request analysis for outgoing requests made with the `aiohttp` client.
  - Adds threat detection and request blocking for aiohttp web applications traced with `ddtrace.contrib.aiohttp.trace_app`. Request bodies sent with chunked transfer encoding or compression, or larger than the application's `client_max_size`, are not inspected.
  - Adds SQL injection protection for byte queries, including `bytearray` and `memoryview` queries, in SQL integrations and Django MySQL backends. Queries are inspected using the connection's encoding, with UTF-8 inspection for PostgreSQL `SQL_ASCII` connections.
- AI Guard
  - Adds an optional `tags` argument to `AIGuardClient.evaluate()`. Each key/value pair in the dictionary is set as a tag on the AI Guard span, so evaluations can be filtered by custom fields in queries, e.g. `client.evaluate(messages, tags={"tenant": "acme"})`. Keys starting with `ai_guard.` are reserved and ignored.
  - Introduces filters and callbacks through middlewares in `ddtrace.aiguard.middleware`, to control which requests AI Guard evaluates and to run custom logic around each evaluation. See the [AI Guard documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/security/ai_guard/) for how to use them.
- algoliasearch
  - This introduces tracing support for `algoliasearch` 3.x.
- elevenlabs
  - Adds LLM Observability support for Python Agents conversations over WebSocket, including conversation audio, transcripts, and client tools. Set `DD_TRACE_ELEVENLABS_ENABLED=false` to disable automatic instrumentation. For improved user-speaking colors, enable `vad_score` in the agent's Advanced settings under Client Events. Audio playback remains available without this optional event.
- pymongo
  - Adds support for PyMongo v4.18
  - Adds Python 3.15 test coverage for current PyMongo releases.
- LLM Observability
  - The agent version set through `LLMObs.agent(version=...)`, `@agent(version=...)`, `LLMObs.annotate(agent={"version": ...})` or `LLMObs.annotation_context(agent={"version": ...})` is now also reported as an `agent_version` tag on child spans of that agent within the same process.
  - The root LLMObs span now includes `http.client_ip` and `network.client.ip` tags when AppSec or `DD_TRACE_CLIENT_IP_ENABLED` is active and the web framework instruments the request. No additional LLMObs configuration is required.
  - add Amazon Nova 2 Sonic support for the asynchronous AWS SDK for Bedrock Runtime. Conversations include per-turn traces, transcripts, text and audio token usage, tool calls, and playable audio, with speech phases for conversation playback and response-latency measurement.
  - The OpenAI integration now reports `ephemeral_30m_input_tokens` and `ephemeral_12h_input_tokens` metrics for Responses API calls.
  - Adds support for tracing OpenAI Decisions API calls (`client.decisions.create`), capturing the input, questions, answers, and token usage.
  - Adds `LLMObs.routing_context()`, a context manager that sends LLM Observability spans and evaluation metrics created within it to other Datadog organizations instead of the configured one. Pass `dd_api_key` (and optionally `dd_site`) to route to one organization, or `targets` to send the same data to several. Routed data is sent directly to the LLM Observability intake; APM spans are not routed.
  - The OpenAI and Anthropic integrations now track server-side tool usage on LLM spans. This includes `web_search_count` for OpenAI Responses API and Anthropic web searches, and `storage_search_count` for OpenAI file searches.
  - Adds support for submitting LLM Observability spans for TypeSafe `system_one` calls, capturing the request and response bodies and token usage. Images are recorded by reference, not by content.
  - OpenAI Decisions API spans and typesafe-sdk System One spans are now tagged with `decision_provider` (`openai` and `typesafe` respectively) to identify decision model spans.
- AWS Bedrock Runtime
  - Adds reported input and output text token counts to Nova Sonic 2 spans in LLM Observability alongside audio token counts.
- OpenAI
  - Adds reported audio, text, image, and cached token counts to Realtime spans in LLM Observability for detailed token breakdowns.
- mcp
  - LLM Observability MCP server spans, including tool call spans, now include the calling client's self-reported name, title, and version as the `mcp_client_name`, `mcp_client_title`, and `mcp_client_version` tags. Tool call spans are not tagged for servers on `mcp<2` using stateless streamable HTTP, where the client's identity is unavailable.
  - Adds support for `mcp` 2.x, including clients and servers using the stateless 2026-07-28 MCP protocol. Previously, no APM or Agent Observability spans were created for MCP clients or servers when `mcp` 2.x was installed.
- tracing
  - Adds `DD_TRACE_HTTP_CLIENT_ERROR_STATUSES` to configure which HTTP client response status codes mark a span as an error when `DD_TRACE_OTEL_SEMANTICS_ENABLED=true`. When it is not set, client status codes of 400 and above are errors.
  - Adds support for OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions on HTTP client spans, enabled with `DD_TRACE_OTEL_SEMANTICS_ENABLED=true`. When enabled, client spans use OpenTelemetry attribute names and low-cardinality resource names; the default remains the existing Datadog behavior.
  - Adds support for OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic conventions on HTTP server spans when `DD_TRACE_OTEL_SEMANTICS_ENABLED=true`.
  - Adds shared OpenTelemetry HTTP span behavior for upcoming client and server integrations, enabled with `DD_TRACE_OTEL_SEMANTICS_ENABLED`. See the [OpenTelemetry API docs](https://ddtrace.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html#module-ddtrace.opentelemetry) for details.
  - Adds gRPC support for OTLP trace export. Set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=grpc` or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` to use gRPC; `http/protobuf` remains the default for traces. Applications that use the global gRPC setting but require HTTP trace export must set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf`. gRPC trace export currently supports plaintext `http://` endpoints only.
- profiling
  - Adds experimental support for installing Profiler's hooks at startup without starting the profiler, so that a profiler can be started later at runtime. This option is disabled by default, is not yet recommended for production use, and its behavior may change in future releases.
- CI visibility
  - Reports whether Test Impact Analysis skipped tests in a suite so affected durations can be excluded from comparisons. This is available for serial runs of the current pytest integration, without requiring code coverage collection.
  - Adds `pytest.mark.dd_prevent_failure_suppression` to override Datadog quarantine and disabling, and `pytest.mark.dd_no_auto_retry` to exclude Datadog automatic retries. Both markers support test functions, classes, modules, and individual parameter cases while preserving explicit pytest plugin retries.
  - the pytest plugin now respects `DD_CIVISIBILITY_GIT_UPLOAD_ENABLED` (matching dd-trace-js and dd-trace-go). When `false`, the git metadata upload is skipped entirely; upload once per pipeline instead (e.g. `datadog-ci git-metadata upload` in a setup job). The pull request merge-base is still computed from local history when possible.
  - The pytest plugin now respects the `DD_CIVISIBILITY_GIT_UNSHALLOW_ENABLED` environment variable (matching `dd-trace-js`). When set to `false`, the plugin never runs `git fetch --shallow-since` on shallow clones; the `/search_commits` check and any pending packfile upload still run using the locally available history.
- typesafe
  - Adds tracing support for `TypeSafeClient.system_one` and `AsyncTypeSafeClient.system_one` calls in the TypeSafe Python SDK (`typesafe-sdk`).

### Security Issues

- internal
  - HTTPS connections made by ddtrace's native components now reject certificate chains that pass through a small set of intermediate certificate authorities distrusted due to security concerns.
- AAP
  - Fixes an issue where building ddtrace from source with Python optimizations enabled (`-O` or `PYTHONOPTIMIZE`) skipped the integrity check of the downloaded libddwaf library. The library is now checked against checksums pinned in ddtrace rather than ones downloaded alongside it.

### Bug Fixes

- AI Guard
  - Fixes an issue where setting `DD_AI_GUARD_TIMEOUT` below `1000` resulted in a request timeout of 0, because the value is applied in whole seconds. Such values now log a warning at startup and fall back to the default of `10000`.
  - Fixes an issue where streamed LangChain chat model and LLM responses were not evaluated when `DD_AI_GUARD_ANALYZE_STREAM_RESPONSES_ENABLED` is `true`. The stream is now read and evaluated before any chunk is returned, and a block returns no chunk.
  - Fixes an issue where, with `DD_AI_GUARD_ANALYZE_STREAM_RESPONSES_ENABLED` set to `true`, a LangChain model that streams delivered tokens to callbacks (for example `astream_events()` or LangGraph `stream_mode="messages"`) before AI Guard evaluated the response. Callbacks now receive the tokens after the evaluation, and none when it blocks.
  - Fixes an issue where the Strands Agents integration raised a `ValueError` when an agent invocation finished in a different asyncio task, and where OpenAI and Anthropic calls in the task that started the invocation were then no longer evaluated.
  - Fixes an issue where streaming OpenAI Responses API calls (`responses.create(stream=True)`) were not evaluated when `DD_AI_GUARD_ANALYZE_STREAM_RESPONSES_ENABLED` was unset or `false`. Request inputs are now evaluated, matching Chat Completions and Anthropic streaming calls, so these calls can now be blocked when blocking is enabled. To keep evaluating without blocking, set `DD_AI_GUARD_BLOCK=false`; to disable AI Guard for OpenAI, set `DD_AI_GUARD_OPENAI_ENABLED=false`.
- aws_lambda
  - Rotates the runtime ID and refreshes registered components when an AWS Lambda MicroVM application starts after restore.
- CI Visibility
  - Fixes excessive CPU usage that could slow down or time out test jobs when Code Coverage is enabled with pytest-xdist.
  - Fixes an issue where pytest test discovery reports success despite collection errors. With `DD_TEST_OPTIMIZATION_DISCOVERY_ENABLED` enabled, collection errors now return exit code 2 while preserving partial discovery results, unless `--continue-on-collection-errors` is supplied.
  - Fixes excessive memory use when generating Code Coverage reports for large projects when using coverage.py, particularly when tests run with multiple workers.
  - Fixes an issue where pytest runs using copied or restored execution contexts (e.g. Django async tests via asgiref's `async_to_sync`) could end with an internal coverage error, or silently lose or misattribute the coverage data of the tests that use them.
  - Fixes an issue where long test error stack traces and messages were cut off at the end, hiding the failing frame and exception message. When `error.stack` or `error.message` exceed 5000 characters, the last 5000 characters are now kept.
  - Fixes pytest sessions being reported as passed instead of skipped when no tests are collected.
  - Fixes repeated Git history fetches that slow down successive `pytest` commands in the same shallow checkout. Fetches are retried when the checked-out commit or shallow history changes.
  - skip the `git fetch --shallow-since` unshallow on shallow clones when the backend already knows all local commits and the pull request merge-base is not needed or user-supplied (`DD_GIT_PULL_REQUEST_BASE_BRANCH_SHA`); shallow-graph merge-bases are untrusted and recomputed.
- profiling
  - Optimizes unwinding async tasks by removing duplicate intermediate data structure creation
  - Fixes an issue where starting a thread blocks forever when the profiler is enabled and the thread name contains a lone surrogate or a null character.
  - Fixes a crash that can happen when a uWSGI process exits while the stack profiler is running, for example a worker started with `--lazy-apps --skip-atexit` or a `--master` process with `--py-call-uwsgi-fork-hooks`.
  - Fixes a crash under uWSGI on Python 3.12+ when the application is loaded in the master process without the `lazy-apps`, `py-call-uwsgi-fork-hooks` or `py-call-osafterfork` option. Native frame attribution and exception profiling are now disabled in these workers. Enable `lazy-apps` or `py-call-uwsgi-fork-hooks` to keep them.
  - fixes a crash where mem profiler state was not reset during shutdown, so allocations during shutdown could cause a crash
  - A crash that could happen at exit when using memory profiling has been fixed.
  - Fixes an issue where exception profiling failed to start when another tool had already claimed the `sys.monitoring` slot used by the profiler, by sharing a single monitoring tool with error tracking and falling back to another free slot when one is taken.
  - Profilers failing to start now clean up after themselves instead of keeping half-initialised resources around.
  - On Python 3.14 and later, prevents stack samples from being attributed to stale Python frames after code objects are replaced.
  - a bug that could raise `RecursionError` when pickling a profiler object has been fixed.
  - Fixes a crash with `failed to intern string: OutOfMemory` when the process runs out of memory while the profiler exports a profile. The profile is now dropped instead.
- botocore
  - Fixes an issue where Data Streams Monitoring did not track SQS messages consumed with a JSON body that is not an object, such as an array, string, or number.
  - Fixes an issue where Data Streams Monitoring under-reported end-to-end latency for pathways that pass through a Kinesis consumer.
- error tracking
  - Fixes an issue where handled exceptions from modules listed in `DD_ERROR_TRACKING_HANDLED_ERRORS_INCLUDE` were not reported on Python 3.12 and later when the first handled exception occurred while the module was still being imported, causing all later handled exceptions from the same module to also be missed.
  - Fixes an issue where an internal handled error reporting failure can interrupt application exception handling on Python 3.12 and later.
- AAP
  - Fixes an issue where services were reported to Datadog as having App and API Protection enabled when it was not active, either because `DD_APPSEC_ENABLED` was unset and AAP had not been activated through Remote Configuration, or because AAP failed to load at startup.
- tracing
  - Fixes an issue where traces that do not match any `DD_TRACE_SAMPLING_RULES` rule and have no service-specific Agent rate are sampled at 100% instead of using the default rate provided by the Datadog Agent.
  - Fixes an issue where stale traces from a previous AWS Lambda MicroVM invocation can be exported or used as parents for spans from a later invocation after a runtime identity refresh.
  - Fixes inconsistent handling of oversized or malformed baggage headers.
  - Fixes an issue where per-integration HTTP settings, such as `config.<integration>.http.trace_headers()`, were ignored when set before the integration was enabled.
  - Reduces delays to tracing and the first `/run` request in AWS Lambda MicroVMs during tracer reconfiguration when trace delivery is slow, and prevents cleanup failures from interrupting reconfiguration or shutdown. Native exporter shutdown can still delay Python threads and send pending trace statistics after identity refresh.
  - Fixes an issue where AWS Lambda invocations without an HTTP URL are assigned an HTTP endpoint when trace resource renaming is enabled.
  - Fixes an issue where `baggage` in `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` is reported as unsupported and ignored.
  - Fixes an issue where OTLP log and metric resources use the deprecated `deployment.environment` attribute instead of `deployment.environment.name` for `DD_ENV`.
  - Fixes a rare `ZeroDivisionError` raised from `span.finish()` when multiple threads write traces concurrently.
  - Fixes an issue where the `dd=` list-member of the W3C `tracestate` header could exceed 256 characters, causing proxies that enforce the W3C limit to drop the whole `tracestate` header.
  - Fixes a memory leak where a `contextvars` copy made inside a `@tracer.wrap` function kept the local variables of the finished call in memory.
  - Reduces the overhead of setting ordinary string-valued span tags.
  - Fixes an issue where service, environment, and version values configured through `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` can differ between traces, logs, and metrics. These unified service tags are now applied consistently across all three signals.
  - When exporting traces over OTLP, the tracing library delegates APM RED metrics computation to the OpenTelemetry Collector or Datadog intake by default.
- aiohttp
  - Fixes an issue where tracing HTTP server requests produces repeated callback errors when keep-alive connections close.
  - Fixes an issue where every request to an application traced with `trace_app` failed with `KeyError: 'disable_stream_timing_for_mem_leak'` when the aiohttp integration was not patched, for example with `DD_TRACE_ENABLED=false`.
  - Fixes an issue where the `http.url` tag of aiohttp server spans lost the percent-encoding of the query string. The `http.query.string` tag now also keeps the percent-encoded query string.
- aiopg
  - Fixes missing query spans for connections created through the public connection factory or connection pools, including use with async context managers. Preserves resource cleanup when connection contexts are closed explicitly or cancelled before use.
- algoliasearch
  - This fix resolves an `IndexError` raised when `collect_query_text` is enabled and the search query is passed as a keyword argument.
  - This fix resolves an issue where applications failed to start when `algoliasearch` 4.0.0 or later was installed, raising `TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class` in Django applications.
- remote_config
  - Fixes an issue where updating or deleting one remote configuration for a service discards the tracing settings, such as sampling rules, tags, and log injection, applied by the other remote configurations that still target it.
  - Fixes an issue where forked worker processes, or processes that enable LLM Observability in agentless mode, keep applying a remote configuration that was removed while they were starting.
- code origin
  - Fixes an issue on Python 3.10 where an exception raised from an async generator decorated with `tracer.wrap()` would surface as `TypeError`.
- internal
  - Fixes an issue where forked child processes hang and never exit, causing memory usage to grow and the parent process to stall, when several threads fork at the same time (for example, `multiprocessing.Process` started from a thread pool).
  - Fixes an issue on Python 3.12 and earlier where a process can hang at exit instead of terminating when `gevent` is installed and remote configuration enables Exception Replay or Dynamic Instrumentation while the application is starting.
  - Fixes an issue where wrapping an obfuscated function (for example PyArmor) on Python 3.15 proceeds into instrumentation setup instead of failing cleanly. Those functions still cannot be instrumented.
  - Fixes an issue on Python 3.10 where inspecting the call stack from ddtrace instrumentation placed on async functions and generators could raise a `TypeError`, silently disabling that instrumentation for the call.
  - Fixes an issue where features that use `sys.monitoring` (such as Error Tracking handled-exception monitoring) could fail to enable with a `ValueError` on Python 3.12 and later when a garbage collection ran during startup.
- dynamic instrumentation
  - Fixes an issue where an application thread could hang indefinitely when probes, Exception Replay, or Code Origin produced data faster than it could be uploaded.
  - Fixes an issue where line probes placed on function or method declarations fail to install.
  - Fixes an `AttributeError` that prevented the Symbol Database from loading on Python versions earlier than 3.9.8.
- elasticsearch
  - Fixes an issue where the Elasticsearch request duration metric is missing from spans when Elasticsearch reports a duration of zero milliseconds.
- falcon
  - Fixes an issue where creating a `falcon.asgi.App` failed with a `TypeError` or `CompatibilityError` when the falcon integration was enabled, for example under `ddtrace-run`. ASGI applications now start normally but are not traced by the falcon integration; wrap them with `ddtrace.contrib.asgi.TraceMiddleware` to trace them.
  - Fixes an issue where creating a `falcon.App` failed when `middleware` was `None`, a single component, a tuple, or passed positionally, and where `falcon.API` applications on Falcon 3 produced duplicate `falcon.request` spans.
  - Fixes an issue where a Falcon application returns a 500 Internal Server Error instead of the intended response when `resp.status` is set to an integer, an `http.HTTPStatus` member, or bytes, or when `resp.status_code` is set (Falcon 4).
- google-adk
  - Fixes an issue where applications using `google-adk` 2.10.0 and later fail to start when tracing is enabled, or start normally but report no tool call or code execution spans. Tool calls and code execution are now traced on all supported `google-adk` versions.
  - Fixes an issue where applications using `google-adk` 2.12.0 fail to start with LLM Observability enabled, or start without tool call and code execution spans otherwise. Tool calls made through `Runner.run_live` are now also traced on `google-adk` 2.12.0.
- graphql
  - Fixes an issue where queries fail with a TypeError when resolver tracing is enabled with graphql-core 3.2.10 or later. Restores resolver tracing for synchronous execution with graphql-core 3.3.
- LangChain
  - Fixes missing IAST command-injection findings in legacy agents provided by langchain-classic, and lost taint propagation when formatting chat prompts with LangChain v1.
  - Fixes AI Guard allowing legacy agent tools to execute before a blocking decision when using langchain-classic and the model response evaluation fails or the agent changes the tool arguments.
- IAST
  - Fixes missing vulnerability findings in response middleware around mounted web applications when nested request spans finish before the enclosing request.
  - Fixes an issue where background tasks or worker threads that outlive a request can affect vulnerability analysis for another request. Also prevents errors in instrumented regular-expression substitutions when a request finishes during taint propagation.
- Code Security (IAST)
  - Fixes a potential process crash when a tainted string subclass changes its taint state from its custom hash method.
  - Fixes an issue where SQL values escaped by PyMySQL 1.2.1 and later are not recognized as sanitized.
  - Fixes an issue where, with IAST enabled, integrations such as OpenAI and Anthropic could remain uninstrumented for the lifetime of the process when IAST instrumented the library and it was imported after a product was enabled at runtime, for example through Remote Configuration.
- LLM Observability
  - Fixes an issue where OpenAI and LiteLLM chat calls could block the application for seconds or longer when a chat message contained `Action:` followed by long content.
  - Fixes an issue where concurrently running OpenAI Agent workflows within the same traced operation can be missing from LLM Observability or report incorrect input/output.
  - Fixes an issue where retrieving Agent-delivered or cached prompts requires `DD_API_KEY` in the application. Fetching other prompts still requires the appropriate API credentials.
  - This fix resolves an issue where `google_genai` and `vertexai` LLM spans did not include `tool_use_prompt_token_count` in the input token count.
  - Fixes an issue where `LLMJudge` with the `anthropic` provider raised `TypeError: Object of type method is not JSON serializable` when the model returned a thinking block before the text block (for example, Claude models with adaptive thinking). The judge now reads the first text block in the response.
  - Fixes a regression introduced in 4.15.2 where LLM Observability spans that were still open when an ASGI request finished (FastAPI, Starlette, Django ASGI) were force-finished at request teardown. Agents and background tasks that intentionally outlive the HTTP request had their spans truncated, and work started afterwards was detached into separate root traces instead of staying nested. Abandoned streams are still reclaimed by `TracedStream`/`TracedAsyncStream` finalization and the stream context managers.
- otel
  - Fixes an issue where OTLP HTTP export requests are incorrectly traced when OpenTelemetry logs or metrics collection is enabled with `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp` 1.45.0 or later.
- opentelemetry
  - Fixes an issue where `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` does not enable OTLP log export.
- telemetry
  - Fixes an issue where telemetry events can be associated with a previous AWS Lambda MicroVM invocation after the runtime identity is refreshed.
- uWSGI
  - Fixes an issue where uWSGI workers can hang at startup when `ddtrace` is imported in the master process and neither `lazy-apps` nor `py-call-uwsgi-fork-hooks` is set.
- vllm
  - Fixes an issue with vLLM \>= 0.20.0 where the integration raised `AttributeError: 'EngineCoreOutput' object has no attribute 'num_cached_tokens'`. This error stopped the vLLM output loop and caused all requests to fail. The integration now also handles tracing errors without interrupting vLLM.
- kafka
  - Fixes an issue where Data Streams Monitoring did not link producers to consumers when `Producer.produce()` was called with `headers` as a list of tuples or as `None`.
- MCP
  - Server tool call spans now use the tool result's error text as the error message instead of a generic `tool resulted in an error` message.
  - Fixes an issue where failed server tool calls are not marked as errors when LLM Observability is disabled.
- pytest
  - Fixes deprecation warnings emitted by the Datadog pytest plugin when running test sessions with pluggy 1.7 or newer (for example, pytest 9.2).
- stats computation
  - restore stats computation status when re-enabling tracing after opting out. Opting out of APM tracing now also correctly disables stats computation.
- Fixes an issue where `logging.captureWarnings(True)` had no effect when running under `ddtrace-run` with gevent installed: warnings were written directly to stderr in the default plain-text format instead of being routed through the `py.warnings` logger.

### Other Changes

- tracing
  - Reduces WSGI response iteration overhead. In an end-to-end traced Flask benchmark, many-chunk streaming responses are about 39% faster per request, while single-body responses are unaffected.
